text: The clinic is open Monday to Friday 9am-6pm and Saturday 10am-4pm, closed Sunday. Located at 123 Main St, Suite 200. Free parking in the rear lot.

Botox (botulinum toxin) smooths dynamic wrinkles like forehead lines and crow's feet. Typical price range is $12-$15 per unit, most patients use 20-40 units. Results appear in 3-7 days and last 3-4 months. No downtime; mild redness possible at injection sites.

Dermal fillers (hyaluronic acid) add volume to lips, cheeks, and jawline, and soften nasolabial folds. Price range is roughly $600-$900 per syringe depending on product and area. Results are immediate and last 6-18 months. Mild swelling/bruising for a few days is common.

Laser treatments offered: hair removal, skin resurfacing, and pigmentation/redness reduction. Pricing varies widely by area and number of sessions, roughly $150-$500 per session; a package discount is available after consultation. A series of 3-6 sessions is typical.
Skin treatments include HydraFacial, chemical peels, and microneedling. Prices range roughly $150-$350 per session. Good for texture, tone, and mild acne scarring.

Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, board-certified dermatologist, 12 years injecting Botox and fillers. Dr. James Alvarez, MD, board-certified in facial plastic surgery, focuses on laser treatments and advanced filler work. Both perform free initial consultations for new patients.

Most injectable treatments cause only mild, brief discomfort — patients describe it as a quick pinch. Numbing cream is available on request. Laser treatments can feel like a rubber band snap; cooling is used throughout.

Botox and fillers have no real downtime — patients typically return to normal activities the same day, avoiding strenuous exercise for 24 hours. Laser treatments may need 1-3 days of redness recovery depending on intensity.

Common, temporary side effects: redness, mild swelling, bruising at the treatment site. Rare side effects are discussed in detail during an in-person consultation with the doctor — the AI receptionist does not provide medical advice or guarantee outcomes.

Before injectables: avoid alcohol and blood-thinning medication (e.g. ibuprofen, fish oil) for 24-48 hours if approved by your physician. After treatment: avoid touching/massaging the area for 24 hours, skip strenuous exercise and saunas for a day, and avoid direct sun exposure.
New patients require a brief in-person or video consultation with a doctor before their first injectable treatment; this can often be scheduled back-to-back with the treatment appointment itself.
